name: Vacant Lots in the Neighborhood (Baltimore resident survey)
description: Faithful replication of the resident survey in Rega-Brodsky, Nilon & Warren (2018), "Balancing urban biodiversity needs and resident preferences for vacant lot management", Sustainability 10(5):1679, built from the authors' complete questionnaire and the eight black-and-white photographs of Baltimore vacant lots in its supplementary material (Figure S1). Participants describe their household and neighborhood involvement, rate each lot from very desirable to very undesirable and say why, mark which lots resemble their neighborhood and which they expect to have pests, crime, drugs or litter, pick lots they would and would not want nearby, rank six possible uses of a vacant lot, and give their view on demolishing vacant buildings and maintaining vacant lots. In the original study 44 Baltimore residents from 28 neighborhoods completed the survey. Differences from the original study: (1) online instead of a mailed/emailed paper questionnaire; (2) the eight lots are rated one at a time in random order rather than on one sheet; (3) the paper's text describes ranking the eight lots, but its published questionnaire asks a desirability rating per lot, which is what this template uses (an average rank can still be derived); (4) "Other: ___" write-in boxes are left out; (5) the rank question checks that each rank is used once. Photographs and questionnaire are used with credit for research and removed if the authors object.
author: Rega-Brodsky, Nilon & Warren

elements.name: lots
elements.title: Desirability of the eight example vacant lots
elements.description: One row per lot (key = lot_A … lot_H, the paper's Figure 4 lots). Value { desirability: 1 = Very desirable, 2 = Somewhat desirable, 3 = Somewhat undesirable, 4 = Very undesirable (questionnaire order), why: free text }. Lots shown one at a time in random order, black-and-white photos from the paper's supplementary questionnaire. Lot origins and settings in the paper: A remnant forest, C and E mowed lawn with trees, B, F, H overgrown, D mowed, G cracked asphalt.

config.description: Faithful replication of the resident survey in Rega-Brodsky, Nilon & Warren (2018), Sustainability 10(5):1679, using the authors' complete questionnaire and the eight black-and-white photographs of Baltimore vacant lots from its supplementary material. Participants describe their household and neighborhood involvement, rate how desirable each lot would be, and say which lots they would or would not want nearby and how a vacant lot should be used.
